legend: Arkady and his friends love playing checkers on an n×n$$$n \times n$$$ field. The rows and the columns of the field are enumerated from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$.

The friends have recently won a championship, so Arkady wants to please them with some candies. Remembering an old parable (but not its moral), Arkady wants to give to his friends one set of candies per each cell of the field: the set of candies for cell (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ will have exactly (i2+j2)$$$(i^2 + j^2)$$$ candies of unique type.

There are m$$$m$$$ friends who deserve the present. How many of these n×n$$$n \times n$$$ sets of candies can be split equally into m$$$m$$$ parts without cutting a candy into pieces? Note that each set has to be split independently since the types of candies in different sets are different.
input: The only line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n≤109$$$1 \le n \le 10^9$$$, 1≤m≤1000$$$1 \le m \le 1000$$$) — the size of the field and the number of parts to split the sets into.
output: Print a single integer — the number of sets that can be split equally.
note: In the first example, only the set for cell (3,3)$$$(3, 3)$$$ can be split equally (32+32=18$$$3^2 + 3^2 = 18$$$, which is divisible by m=3$$$m=3$$$).

这些朋友最近赢得了一项锦标赛，因此 Arkady 想送给他们一些糖果作为礼物。想起一个古老的寓言(但不记得其中的寓意)，Arkady 想要为棋盘上的每个格子各准备一份糖果：格子 (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ 中的糖果数量恰好为 (i2+j2)$$$(i^2 + j^2)$$$，且糖果的种类各不相同。
有 m$$$m$$$ 位朋友应当收到这份礼物。棋盘上的 n×n$$$n \times n$$$ 份糖果中，有多少份可以在不将糖果切成小块的情况下，平均分成 m$$$m$$$ 份？注意，由于不同糖果集合中的糖果种类不同，因此每份糖果都必须独立分配。
